memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them on the road through the
Philistine country, though that was shorter. For God said, 'If they face war,
they might change their minds and return to Egypt.'" - Ex 13:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
There was a shorter road. God knew about it, and He deliberately did not take
them that way.

Read the reason again: "If they face war, they might change their minds and
return to Egypt." God was not testing them beyond what they could bear. He was
protecting a people who had been slaves all their lives and had no experience of
battle. He knew exactly how much they could handle, and He routed them around
what would have broken them.

This is one of the most comforting verses in Exodus. The long way round was
mercy.

We rarely see it that way at the time. When the journey takes years longer than
we expected, when the direct route closes, our instinct is to assume God has
lost interest or that we have failed somewhere. Sometimes the delay is exactly
what is keeping us.

Paul writes that God "will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear"
(1 Cor 10:13). God knows our actual strength, not our imagined strength.

The shortest path is not always the kindest one. Sometimes the detour is the
care.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What long road are you on that you have assumed is a failure?
2. Can you thank God for a door He closed that you wanted opened?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You know what I can bear better than I do. Help me to trust the longer
road when You choose it, and to see Your care in the delay. Amen.
